facts.statement: The genus Atychodracon was formally established by Smith in 2015.
facts.quote: authority: Smith, 2015

facts.statement: The only known species, Atychodracon megacephalus, was originally named in 1846 as a species of Plesiosaurus.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Atychodracon megacephalus, named in 1846 originally as a species of Plesiosaurus.

facts.statement: The original holotype specimen was destroyed in a World War II air raid in 1940, leading to the designation of a neotype.
facts.quote: The holotype of "P." megacephalus was destroyed during a World War II air raid in 1940 and was later replaced with a neotype.

facts.statement: Samuel Stutchbury first described and named the type species in January 1846, initially placing it in the genus Plesiosaurus.
facts.quote: The type species of Atychodracon was first described and named by Samuel Stutchbury in January 1846, as a species of the wastebasket taxon Plesiosaurus.

facts.statement: The species name megacephalus translates to "large-headed," referring to the skull's large size relative to the rest of the skeleton.
facts.quote: The specific name means "large-headed" in Greek in reference to the very large skull compared to the rest of the skeletal elements

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is identified as BRSMG Cb 2335, along with its surviving casts and digital models.
facts.quote: The holotype of Atychodracon is BRSMG Cb 2335 and its casts and digital reproductions.

facts.statement: The original holotype skeleton was complete and articulated, measuring 4.960 meters in total length.
facts.quote: BRSMG Cb 2335 represented a complete and articulated skeleton including the skull and lower jaw measuring 4.960 meters in total body length

facts.statement: The holotype was collected from the Blue Lias Formation near Street-on-the-Fosse, Somerset, England.
facts.quote: BRSMG Cb 2335, was collected from the Blue Lias Formation at the Street-on-the-Fosse village, located about 14 km northeast of Street, Somerset, England.

facts.statement: The holotype dates to the earliest Hettangian stage, approximately 201 million years ago.
facts.quote: the area around Street probably originates below the first occurrence of Psiloceras planorbis ammonoid zone (pre-Planorbis beds), in the Psiloceras tilmanni Zone that immediately follows the Triassic-Jurassic boundary, meaning that an earliest Hettangian age is most likely for the specimen, about 201 million years ago.

facts.statement: The original holotype skeleton was destroyed on November 24, 1940, during a World War II air raid.
facts.quote: BRSMG Cb 2335 was destroyed during a World War II air raid on 24 November 1940

facts.statement: At least three casts of the holotype exist, housed in museums in London, Dublin, and Nottingham.
facts.quote: Additionally, at least three casts are known, including: NHMUK R1309/1310 housed at the Natural History Museum, London, TCD.47762a+b at the Geology Museum, Trinity College Dublin, and BGS GSM 118410 at British Geological Survey, Keyworth, Nottingham.

facts.statement: A complete skeleton nicknamed "The Barrow Kipper" is housed at the New Walk Museum in Leicester.
facts.quote: LEICS G221.1851, nicknamed "The Barrow Kipper", represents a complete and well preserved skeleton housed at the New Walk Museum in Leicester

facts.statement: A 2015 revision determined that a neotype was unnecessary because existing casts of the holotype were sufficient to define the species.
facts.quote: However, a 2015 revision of "P." megacephalus pointed out that according to International Code of Zoological Nomenclature article 51.1, designating a neotype in this case is not required since representations of the holotype exist, and are enough to define the species objectively.

facts.statement: Two additional partial skeletons from Street and Barrow-upon-Soar are housed at the National Museum of Ireland.
facts.quote: Two additional specimens, both housed at the National Museum of Ireland, are currently referable to A. megacephalus - NMING F10194, a partial skeleton that includes the skull but not the lower jaw from Street, and NMING F8749, a partial skeleton that includes a damaged skull and suffers from pyrite decay, from Barrow-upon-Soar.

facts.statement: A complete skeleton from Wilmcote, Warwickshire, may represent a new, unnamed rhomaleosaurid species related to Atychodracon.
facts.quote: WARMS 10875, a complete skeleton from Wilmcote, Warwickshire was referred to "P." megacephalus in older publications, e.g. Cruickshank (1994a). However, based on its distinctive morphology and the results of a preliminary phylogenetic analysis, WARMS 10875 seems to represent a new unnamed rhomaleosaurid species potentially related to Atychodracon and Eurycleidus.

facts.statement: Atychodracon lived during the Late Triassic to Early Jurassic boundary in England.
facts.quote: Atychodracon is an extinct genus of rhomaleosaurid plesiosaurian known from the Late Triassic - Early Jurassic boundary (probably early Hettangian stage) of England.

facts.statement: Atychodracon was a medium-sized carnivorous plesiosaur reaching lengths of 5 to 5.29 meters.
facts.quote: Atychodracon is a medium size carnivorous plesiosaurian, known from several individuals of about 5 - 5.29 m in total body length.

facts.statement: Atychodracon possessed a relatively large skull, accounting for 16% of its total body length.
facts.quote: Among such early plesiosaurs, Atychodracon had a relatively large skull with the skull being 16% of its total length.

facts.statement: The snout of Atychodracon had a premaxillary section that was roughly equal in width and length, containing five teeth.
facts.quote: The premaxillary part of its snout is about equal in width and length with five premaxillary teeth.

facts.statement: Based on the holotype, Atychodracon had 29 to 30 neck vertebrae and approximately 32 tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Atychodracon, based solely on the holotype, has 29-30 neck vertebrae including the atlas bone and axis, about 32 tail vertebrae

facts.statement: Recent studies indicate little close relationship between Atychodracon and true Rhomaleosaurus species, sharing only general rhomaleosaurid traits.
facts.quote: Recent studies find little kinship between Atychodracon and true Rhomaleosaurus spp., aside from traits that are shared between most rhomaleosaurids.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Atychodracon is closely related to Eurycleidus, as some analyses support a sister-taxon relationship while others do not.
facts.quote: Yet, this is not supported by all analyses, and despite the difficulty in directly comparing the two, several differences exist.

facts.statement: The lower jaw symphysis of Atychodracon was expanded to the sides, with the width nearly equal to its length.
facts.quote: The mandibular symphysial region is expanded to the sides, nearly equal in width and length.

facts.statement: The holotype of P. megacephalus was destroyed during an air raid in 1940 and later replaced by a neotype.
facts.quote: El holotipo de "P". megacephalus fue destruido durante un ataque aéreo de la Segunda Guerra Mundial en 1940 y luego fue reemplazado por un neotipo.

facts.statement: Atychodracon is an extinct genus of rhomaleosaurid plesiosaur known from the Late Triassic–Early Jurassic boundary (likely early Hettangian stage) of England.
facts.quote: Atychodracon es un género extinto de plesiosaurio romaleosáurido conocido del límite Triásico Superior - Jurásico Inferior (probablemente piso Hettangiense temprano) de Inglaterra.

facts.statement: The species had an unstable taxonomic history, being referred to four different genera by various authors until a new genus name was created in 2015.
facts.quote: La especie tenía una historia taxonómica muy inestable, siendo referida a cuatro géneros diferentes por varios autores hasta que se creó un nuevo nombre de género en 2015.

facts.statement: The genus Atychodracon was established by Smith in 2015.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Smith, 2015

facts.statement: The type species Atychodracon megacephalus was originally named by Stutchbury in 1846.
facts.quote: type_species_authority: Stutchbury, 1846

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses found "R." megacephalus to be basal to the clade containing Rhomaleosaurus and Eurycleidus, supporting its placement in its own genus.
facts.quote: Cladistic analyses by Ketchum & Benson, 2010, Benson et al., 2011, Ketchum & Benson, 2011, and various later studies found "R." megacephalus to be basal to the clade containing Rhomaleosaurus and Eurycleidus, thus it should be in its own genus as suggested by Smith and Dyke (2008).

facts.statement: Besides the destroyed holotype and its three surviving partial molds, a neotype and two additional individuals are currently referred to Atychodracon megacephalus, making it a relatively well-represented rhomaleosaurid.
facts.quote: Además del holotipo destruido y sus tres moldes parciales (que sobrevivieron), un neotipo y dos individuos adicionales se refieren actualmente a Atychodracon megacephalus, lo que lo convierte en un romaleosáurido relativamente bien representado.

facts.statement: Samuel Stutchbury described the type species of Atychodracon in January 1846 as a species of the wastebasket taxon Plesiosaurus.
facts.quote: La especie tipo de Atychodracon fue descrita y nombrada por primera vez por Samuel Stutchbury en enero de 1846, como una especie del taxón cajón de sastre Plesiosaurus.

facts.statement: The species name means "large head" in Greek, referring to the skull being very large compared to the rest of the skeletal elements of "Plesiosaurus" megalocephalus.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie significa "cabeza grande" en griego en referencia al cráneo muy grande en comparación con el resto de los elementos esqueléticos que tenía "Plesiosaurus" megalocephalus

facts.statement: The plesiosauroid nature of "Plesiosaurus" megalocephalus remained unnoticed until a review by Richard Lydekker in 1889.
facts.quote: La naturaleza pliosauroidea de "Plesiosaurus" megalocephalus permaneció inadvertida hasta una revisión de Richard Lydekker en 1889.

facts.statement: The holotype of Atychodracon is BRSMG Cb 2335 and its molds and digital reproductions.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Atychodracon es BRSMG Cb 2335 y sus moldes y reproducciones digitales.

facts.statement: The holotype BRSMG Cb 2335 represented a complete articulated skeleton including the skull and lower jaw that measured 4.960 meters in total body length.
facts.quote: BRSMG Cb 2335 representó un esqueleto completo y articulado que incluía el cráneo y la mandíbula inferior que medía 4.960 metros de longitud corporal total

facts.statement: The holotype BRSMG Cb 2335 was collected from the Blue Lias Formation in the village of Street-on-the-Fosse, located about 14 km northeast of Street, Somerset, England.
facts.quote: BRSMG Cb 2335, se recolectó de la Formación Blue Lias en el pueblo de Street-on-the-Fosse, ubicado a unos 14 km al noreste de Street, Somerset, Inglaterra.

facts.statement: The Blue Lias, also known as the Lower Lias, dates to the Upper Triassic-Lower Jurassic boundary, including the Rhaetian, Hettangian, and lower Sinemurian stages.
facts.quote: El Blue Lias, también conocido como el Lias Inferior, se remonta al límite del Triásico Superior - Jurásico Inferior, por lo que incluye las etapas Rhaetiense, Hettangiense y Sinemuriense inferior.

facts.statement: However, it is possible that some specimens from the area originate from slightly younger deposits.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, es posible que algunos de los especímenes del área provengan de depósitos un poco más jóvenes.

facts.statement: BRSMG Cb 2335 was destroyed during an air raid of the Second World War on November 24, 1940.
facts.quote: BRSMG Cb 2335 fue destruido durante un ataque aéreo de la Segunda Guerra Mundial el 24 de noviembre de 1940

facts.statement: Cruickshank (1994a) described LEICS G221.1851 as the neotype specimen for "P." megacephalus due to the destruction of BRSMG Cb 2335.
facts.quote: Cruickshank (1994a) describió LEICS G221.1851 como espécimen de neotipo para "P". megacephalus debido a la destrucción de BRSMG Cb 2335.

facts.statement: LEICS G221.1851, nicknamed "The Barrow Kipper", represents a complete and well-preserved skeleton housed in the New Walk Museum in Leicester.
facts.quote: LEICS G221.1851, apodado "The Barrow Kipper", representa un esqueleto completo y bien conservado alojado en el Museo New Walk en Leicester

facts.statement: However, a 2015 review of "P." megacephalus noted that according to the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature, article 51.1, a neotype does not need to be designated in this case since representations of the holotype exist and are sufficient to define the species objectively.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, una revisión de 2015 de "P". megacephalus señaló que según el Código Internacional de Nomenclatura Zoológica, artículo 51.1, no se requiere designar un neotipo en este caso ya que existen representaciones del holotipo, y son suficientes para definir la especie de manera objetiva.

facts.statement: Atychodracon is a medium-sized carnivorous plesiosaur, known from several individuals about 5 meters in total body length, with skulls measuring around 80 cm.
facts.quote: Atychodracon es un plesiosaurio carnívoro de tamaño mediano, conocido por varios individuos de unos 5 metros de longitud total del cuerpo, con cráneos que miden alrededor de 80 cm.

facts.statement: Among these early plesiosaurs, Atychodracon had a relatively large skull, accounting for 16% of its total length.
facts.quote: Entre estos primeros plesiosaurios, Atychodracon tenía un cráneo relativamente grande, con un cráneo del 16% de su longitud total.

facts.statement: The premaxillary part of its snout has approximately the same width and length with five premaxillary teeth.
facts.quote: La parte premaxilar de su hocico tiene aproximadamente el mismo ancho y largo con cinco dientes premaxilares.

facts.statement: Based solely on the holotype, Atychodracon has 29-30 cervical vertebrae, including the atlas and axis, and around 32 tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Atychodracon, basado únicamente en el holotipo, tiene 29-30 vértebras del cuello, incluido el atlas y el eje, alrededor de 32 vértebras de la cola

facts.statement: Atychodracon shows a more robust humerus and an inverse relationship in the radius to the length of the ulna.
facts.quote: Atychodracon muestra un húmero más robusto, y una relación inversa en el radio a la longitud del cúbito.

facts.statement: Among other romaleosaurids, Atychodracon material has been referred mainly to two genera before its separation, namely Rhomaleosaurus and Eurycleidus.
facts.quote: Entre otros romaleosáuridos, el material de Atychodracon se ha referido principalmente a dos géneros antes de su separación, a saber, Rhomaleosaurus y Eurycleidus.

facts.statement: However, this is not supported by all analyses, and despite the difficulty of comparing them directly, there are several differences.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, esto no está respaldado por todos los análisis y, a pesar de la dificultad de compararlos directamente, existen varias diferencias.

facts.statement: The holotype of Eurycleidus lacks a skull, and the previously referred OUM J.28585 probably represents a new taxon, so there is little overlapping material between the holotypes of Atychodracon and Eurycleidus.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Eurycleidus carece de cráneo, y el OUM J.28585 anteriormente referido probablemente representa un nuevo taxón, por lo que existe poco material superpuesto entre los holotipos de Atychodracon y Eurycleidus.

facts.statement: In Eurycleidus, the midline notch on the lower surface of the mandibular symphysis is not bordered by posterior splenials, as in Atychodracon.
facts.quote: En Eurycleidus, la hendidura de la línea media en la superficie inferior de la sínfisis mandibular no está bordeada por los esplenios de la parte posterior, como en Atychodracon.

facts.statement: Unlike the straight preaxial margin of the humerus in Atychodracon, it is concave in Eurycleidus.
facts.quote: A diferencia del margen preaxial recto del húmero de Atychodracon, es cóncavo en Eurycleidus.

facts.statement: These distinctions suggest that, while Atychodracon is quite related to Eurycleidus, it represents a separate genus.
facts.quote: Estas distinciones sugieren que, si bien Atychodracon está bastante relacionado con Eurycleidus, representa un género separado.

facts.statement: The genus Atychodracon was erected in 2015 by Smith to include the species Atychodracon megacephalus.
facts.quote: Smith erigió el nuevo nombre de género Atychodracon en 2015 para "R". megacephalus, siendo la especie tipo Atychodracon megacephalus.

facts.statement: The genus name Atychodracon is derived from the Greek word for 'unfortunate', referring to the destruction of the holotype during an air raid in 1940.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del griego ατυχής, atychis, que significa "desafortunado" en referencia a la desafortunada destrucción del holotipo durante un bombardeo aéreo de la Segunda Guerra Mundial en 1940

facts.statement: In many phylogenetic analyses, Atychodracon has frequently been included under the name Rhomaleosaurus megacephalus.
facts.quote: Atychodracon ha sido incluido en muchas ocasiones en diversos análisis filogenéticos, generalmente como "Rhomaleosaurus" megacephalus.

facts.statement: Atychodracon belongs to the family Rhomaleosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Rhomaleosauridae

facts.statement: Atychodracon is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
